articles.title: “I just want to share that with all these little kids”: How Sophie Cunningham's $10,182 act of kindness turned WNBA frustration into a heartwarming moment for families in need
articles.summary: NBA News: Sophie Cunningham had plenty of reasons to be frustrated in 2025. The Indiana Fever guard picked up multiple WNBA fines before a knee injury ended her.
articles.body: Sophie Cunningham had plenty of reasons to be frustrated in 2025. The Indiana Fever guard picked up multiple WNBA fines before a knee injury ended her season early. But a joke she made during that stretch took an unexpected turn. What started as a GoFundMe for fines or even a yacht raised $10,182. Cunningham then chose to give the money to a cause that had already touched her life.Sophie Cunningham turned her WNBA fines joke into a $10,182 act of kindnessOn Oct. 2, 2025, Sophie Cunningham launched a GoFundMe with a $26,000 goal. The Indiana Fever guard kept things playful when she explained the reason behind it.“This is more of a joke than anything. For fines only or to charity or for a yacht idk…,” Cunningham wrote on the GoFundMe page.The joke quickly caught on with her supporters. Over the next five days, 171 people donated to the fundraiser. Contributions ranged from $5 to $2,699, and the total eventually reached $10,182.That was when Cunningham decided the money would take a different path. “A yacht would be nice, but whatever we raise here will be going directly to Ronald McDonald House Charities. I’ll take care of my own fines. Y’all are the best,” Cunningham wrote in an update on the GoFundMe page, according to the Indianapolis Star's Oct. 10, 2025 report.The decision came after a season in which Cunningham had become increasingly vocal about her frustrations with the WNBA. She had received multiple fines after speaking publicly about league officiating.In an August episode of her podcast, Show Me Something, Sophie Cunningham explained her disciplinary record with a joke of her own.“I’m officially 3-for-3 on being fined by the WNBA,” she said during the episode.She also explained why she continued to speak out, saying, “I promise you, everyone in our league feels that way and I’m just kind of the only one who says something.”So the fundraiser made sense at the moment. Sophie Cunningham had joked about the fines, fans responded and the money started coming in. Yet when she had more than $10,000 sitting in the fundraiser, she did not use it to erase the fines that had inspired the idea.Instead, she picked Ronald McDonald House Charities. That choice also came during a difficult personal stretch. Cunningham's 2025 season ended on Aug. 17 after she tore the MCL in her right knee. She later spent time on the sideline alongside several injured Fever teammates, including Caitlin Clark and Sydney Colson.During the Fever's exit interviews, Cunningham made it clear that she planned to return strong. When reporters asked whether she expected to be healthy for the 2026 season, she answered, “Hell yeah, man,” before saying she hoped to ramp up basketball activities in January.The fundraiser gave Cunningham a chance to do something positive while she waited for her own return.Sophie Cunninghum past Ronald McDonald House connection goes back to 2015The charity was not just any random act. Sophie Cunningham first encountered Ronald McDonald House Charities as a teenager.Ronald McDonald House Charities helps families stay close to their children while they receive medical treatment. Its programmes provide places to stay, meals and other support for families facing difficult medical situations. Cunningham’s donation therefore went toward a cause that helps families during some of the hardest moments of their lives.On 2015, the Columbia Missourian reported on Cunningham's visit to a Ronald McDonald House in Chicago while she prepared for the McDonald's All-American Game. She met Brian and Jennifer Godish and their four-year-old son, Bradley, who had leukemia. Cunningham played with Bradley, built wooden train tracks with him and joined other children for basketball. She also volunteered to visit children who could not leave the hospital.“It makes me smile because this is how my parents raised me, and I’m just a little bit of who they are. I just want to share that with all these little kids and their parents,” Cunningham told the Columbia Missourian during that 2015 visit.Ten years later, she was once again giving to the same organisation. This time, her fans helped her raise the money.What began as a joke about WNBA fines ended with Sophie Cunningham choosing kindness over keeping the money for herself, adding a meaningful chapter to a connection that started long before her Indiana Fever career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Luka Doncic gives first Lakers roster outlook after spending $18,000 an hour flight for teammates: See Photos
articles.summary: NBA News: Luka Doncic has made his first major statement as the undisputed face of the Los Angeles Lakers. With LeBron James gone after joining the Philadelphia.
articles.body: Luka Doncic has made his first major statement as the undisputed face of the Los Angeles Lakers. With LeBron James gone after joining the Philadelphia 76ers, Doncic brought the Lakers to Slovenia for a four-day minicamp designed to build chemistry before his first full season as the franchise's centerpiece. He welcomed his teammates with dinner, workouts, pickup games, golf and time exploring Ljubljana, turning an offseason trip into an early test of his leadership.Luka Doncic gives first Lakers roster outlook in LeBron James-less eraThe itinerary mixed basketball with leisure. The players worked out, played pickup games, visited Lake Bled for fishing, played golf and explored Ljubljana. Dinner at Doncic's favorite restaurant was also part of the trip.Doncic's Instagram Story captured the start of the gathering with a simple caption: “First supper,” Doncic wrote.The Lakers enter the 2026-27 season with Doncic at the center of everything. James' departure ended a defining chapter in Los Angeles, while Doncic's first full season as the team's unquestioned leader begins with a roster built around his offensive game.Doncic's production gives the Lakers plenty to build on. He led the league with 33.5 points per game in 2025-26 while averaging 8.3 assists, 7.7 rebounds and 1.6 steals. He shot 47.6% from the field and 36.6% from 3-point range.Los Angeles also made significant moves around him. The Lakers retained Austin Reaves on a four-year, $185 million contract and acquired Walker Kessler from the Utah Jazz through a sign-and-trade. Kessler received a four-year, $130 million deal, while the Lakers also sent two unprotected first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps in the transaction.Quentin Grimes, Collin Sexton, Sandro Mamukelashvili, Kevon Looney, Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams were among the other additions. It appears that the Lakers are constructing a roster intended to maximize Doncic's strengths.Luka Doncic reportedly spent $18,000 an hour for teammatesThe trip also came with a remarkable price tag. Doncic reportedly chartered a Bombardier Global 8000 for 14 Lakers players, with the 13-hour flight costing at least $18,000 per hour. The 26-hour round trip is expected to cost roughly $500,000, according to Slovenian outlet 24ur.com, with Doncic covering the expense.Doncic's leadership has not been limited to roster decisions. The Slovenia trip gave him a chance to create the kind of shared experience that can be difficult to manufacture during an NBA season.The 14 players reportedly traveled aboard a luxurious Bombardier Global 8000. Images from the flight showed a lounge area, individual bedrooms, beds, couches, recliners and televisions. After arriving, Doncic met his teammates alongside his daughter, Gabriela.The Lakers need their new hierarchy to work on the court, but Doncic also needs to establish himself inside a locker room that previously revolved around James.The Lakers are building the roster around DoncicThis is not Doncic's first attempt at bringing his teammates together. He organized a Porsche Driving Experience for the Lakers in October 2025, shortly after joining the organization.This minicamp carries more weight. James is no longer there, and Doncic now enters the season without another established superstar occupying the franchise's leadership role.The Lakers are also dealing with significant organizational change. Mark Walter's $12.5 billion purchase of the team and the Buss family's dispute over its remaining stakes have added another layer of uncertainty around the franchise.Doncic has so far handled that backdrop while remaining focused on basketball. The Slovenia minicamp gives him an opportunity to set the tone before training camp and the regular season arrive.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Lakers Must Pursue Naz Reid Trade To Give Luka Chance at Championship amid Latest NBA Rumors
articles.summary: If the Los Angeles Lakers get involved with the upcoming iteration of NBA trade season, they need to find ways of stretching their trade budget.
articles.body:
If the Los Angeles Lakers get involved with the upcoming iteration of NBA trade season, they need to find ways of stretching their trade budget.

They haven't exhausted their asset collection, but they're pretty close after the costly sign-and-trade for Walker Kessler this summer. So, in a perfect world, they'd find a reasonably priced pickup capable of checking multiple boxes.

Perhaps this single-stone-for-multiple-birds pursuit could steer them toward Charlotte Hornets combo big Naz Reid, who has a "very high" chance of getting traded, per The Athletic's Jon Krawczynski . Or rather, that should probably say steer them back toward Reid, since they "called" on his availability over the offseason, per Dan Woike of The Athletic.

If the Lakers can afford a Reid trade, that would be worth the piggy bank-bursting splurge to get him.

They probably need the Hornets to be big fans of Cameron Carr or Adou Thiero (or both) for a trade to materialize, but that feels possible if Charlotte opts to lean harder into a youth movement around Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel. Especially with things off to a less-than-ideal start for Reid and for the Hornets as a whole (4-9 with a minus-11.1 net rating , per NBA.com).

In a better basketball situation, though, Reid could flourish.

The 6'9", 264-pounder pairs perimeter finesse with paint force. What that means is he could be the stretchy scoring presence they need at the 4 spot while also shoring up that problematic backup big man role.

He was a supersub (and one-time Sixth Man of the Year) on some high-level Minnesota Timberwolves teams. Reid might be even better positioned to flourish with the Lakers, as they feature even more creation and playmaking with the backcourt combo of Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves.

Reid can be an all-purpose screen-setter, since he can shred nets from distance or explode to (and above) the rim off of hard rolls. He can find open teammates on quick, simple, gear-turning passes. He can rebound and protect the paint.

In short, he has that coveted across-the-board skill set that every team seeks in its supporting cast.

Trade cost is a consideration, obviously, but it's hard to imagine Reid's would be overwhelming. He is shooting just 39.9 percent from the field and has never been a full-time starter prior to this season.

He is a rock-solid contributor, but he might be overpaid in the second season of a five-year, $125 million pact. The Lakers should be conscious of that, but as long as that gets factored into his trade price, that's probably something they could stomach.

They just have to believe the on-court upgrade is worth it. Given the obvious overlap between his skills and their wish list, that shouldn't be the hardest sell.

And they should have some leverage in these talks. As proud owners of a red-hot 12-2 record, they don't need Reid on this roster. One could argue they shouldn't feel the need to look outside the organization for any kind of help.

Remember, though, their aim goes way beyond first-month domination. If they want to convert this sizzling start into sustained success come playoff time, then their front office needs to be nitpicky while holding this roster to the highest possible standard.

Through those elevated expectations, L.A. probably can sense a few needs. Like more scoring from the forward spots. And a lot more reliability and impact out of its backup center.

Reid is capable of scratching both itches. In fact, he might be the most capable of doing so among all trade candidates they could realistically afford.

articles.title: Bam Adebayo Talks GTA 6-Inspired NBA 2K27 Cover, Rating, Giannis, Heat and More in B/R Interview
articles.summary: Miami Heat star center Bam Adebayo has made no secret of how much he was influenced by the late Kobe Bryant, and he's following in his idol's footsteps once again.
articles.body:
Miami Heat star center Bam Adebayo has made no secret of how much he was influenced by the late Kobe Bryant, and he's following in his idol's footsteps once again.

After surpassing Bryant's iconic 81-point game with an 83-point performance last season, Adebayo joined the Black Mamba and many other greats as the cover star of the NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition, a new collaboration with Rockstar Games ahead of Thursday's highly anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto VI.

"Man, I grew up playing this game wholeheartedly. Just to be part of 2K, I got that chance, but also now I get to see myself on a cover. You know, because a lot of our idols were on the cover of 2K, like mine was Kobe," Adebayo told Bleacher Report. "To see Kobe on the front of a cover was like, 'Yo, this is his game.' So, to have that moment to be a part of it and to be the cover is just, it's surreal."

The NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition is available digitally from Nov. 27 through Jan. 15 across PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC via Steam. The extended, seven-week Season 3 will include fresh content such as a brand-new Vice City-inspired park in The City, Vice City-themed rewards and apparel, and more.

The Heat will be celebrating the release of Grand Theft Auto VI in Wednesday's home game against the Milwaukee Bucks, dubbed "A Night in Vice City." Adebayo and his teammates will be wearing special-edition Nike x Cactus Jack uniforms that can now be found in NBA 2K27.

As a nine-year veteran who has spent his entire career in Miami, Adebayo was excited to see South Beach under the spotlight.

"I take no credit, obviously, because it's Miami, but like, if you lived in this city, you understand how great this city really is," he said. "To be a part of Vice City and to know the history, you never really have a bad day, besides the rain. Every once in a while, we get some rain, but to be in the middle of January and it's 80 degrees, you can't put it into words. There's always something to do here, it's just an active city."

After being revealed as NBA 2K's newest cover star, Adebayo joked that he has to do some lobbying to get his 87 overall rating bumped up. While he doesn't have much time for video games during the NBA season, he said he plans to hone his skills so he can hold his own against the youngsters in the Heat locker room.

"I don't know, man. I guess just have a conversation with Ronnie at this point. I'll be like, man, you can give me at least a 90," he said with a laugh. "But it is what it is, I don't get too mad about it. To me, for what the young kids say, I'm actually nice in 2K. My build, apparently I got the best build, low-key. But the game is too advanced now. So, I play when I can, but the shot meter all quick and everything. Now I'm like, 'Hold on, man!'"

Miami started the 2026-27 season with four straight losses but has since found a groove, carrying a 7-6 record and a four-game win streak into Monday night's game against the Houston Rockets (11-3). Adebayo said the team's slow start wasn't a surprise after the integration of so many new faces, led by two-time NBA MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo.

"We're starting to figure stuff out, but we still got a long way to go," he said. "Obviously, it's a new team, everybody's still trying to adjust to one another, figure out how to mesh the way we play together, and how we try to get a flow as much as possible throughout the game to where it's consistent."

Adebayo's new partnership with Antetokounmpo has been rocky at times, and the big man's numbers have dropped slightly while trying to adjust to his new running mate. Legends like former Heat star Udonis Haslem and Hall of Famer Kevin Garnett have recently called out Adebayo for his play this season, but the 29-year-old knows they simply want to bring the best out of him.

"Speaking on UD, that's somebody I talk to every day. So it's not like it's a shot at me, but it's like I'm hearing a familiar voice, as always. So he's doing that because he cares," he said. "For KG, he was a role model of mine. I looked up to KG. So to hear somebody that I looked up to set a certain expectation and a standard for me, you look at it as he sees your potential."

In addition to learning Antetokounmpo on the court, Adebayo said he's still adjusting to not seeing him as an opponent.

"For me, it was getting used to being around him because we've always competed against each other. So every time I saw him, it was more like I'm in competition mode; I'm intense, ready to compete," Adebayo said. "And now I got to get used to just seeing him, like I'm going to my treatment time, and I see him. Like, you still got to adjust. But the most part is just getting to know him. That's really what it is."

He added: "I'm still getting used to how much he talks. Not saying he's just a Chatty Cathy, but to just have a conversation with him. He's very vocal, and then obviously we get on the court and behind the scenes when we're watching film, he's very vocal in those settings."

Antetokounmpo's arrival has surely raised expectations in Miami, and Adebayo isn't shying away from championship expectations. However, he's not getting ahead of himself, and he wants the Heat's identity to be a hard-nosed defensive team, which would help everything else fall into place.

"I think for us to be successful, I want us to be a top-three defense in this league, because it leads to all our strengths," he said. "Giannis in transition, Davion [Mitchell] in transition. Obviously, people are trying to find Klay [Thompson] in transition. Everybody's playing downhill, and that causes havoc for other teams."

articles.title: JJ Redick Calls Out Lakers' Struggles Despite Luka Doncic, LA's 12-2 Record After Win vs. Suns
articles.summary: Despite improving to 12-2 with Sunday's 131-123 win over the Phoenix Suns, Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick isn't happy with his team.
articles.body:
Despite improving to 12-2 with Sunday's 131-123 win over the Phoenix Suns, Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick isn't happy with his team.

Per The Athletic's Law Murray , Reddick called out the Lakers for their defensive lapses, particularly late in games.

"I told the team this after the game — we're working too hard, and we're playing too hard, to build these leads — it's a disservice to each other to take your foot off the gas," Redick said after the Lakers were outscored 43-27 in the fourth quarter. "I thought defensively, (we) did a lot of really good things through three quarters. Going to the fourth, we got a 107 defensive rating, and then we have a 165 defensive rating in the fourth. I believe we can be a good defensive team. This has been consistent now — this is a trend. Gotta be better in the fourth quarter."

Lakers star guard Luka Doncic put on another scintillating performance with 43 points and nine assists to lead Los Angeles to its eighth straight win.

While the Lakers are now tied for the best record in the Western Conference, Redick is right to point out that the way his team is playing is untenable. Los Angeles has given up over 100 points in nine of its last 10 games, including in every game during this current win streak.

The Lakers won't be able to rely on simply putting up big offensive numbers every night, especially when things get tighter in the playoffs. Los Angeles will have to find consistency on defense if it hopes to compete for an NBA title this year.

The Lakers will try to follow Redick's direction as they seek their ninth straight win on Tuesday against the Charlotte Hornets (4-9).

articles.title: New NBA Trade Rumors on Trey Murphy's Wild Asking Price from Pelicans amid Dejounte, Zion Buzz
articles.summary: New Orleans Pelicans small forward Trey Murphy III has been floated as a potential trade target ahead of the NBA's trade deadline in February, but teams may find it difficult to acquire him.
articles.body:
New Orleans Pelicans small forward Trey Murphy III has been floated as a potential trade target ahead of the NBA's trade deadline in February, but teams may find it difficult to acquire him.

During Monday's episode of the Hoop Collective, ESPN's Brian Windhorst and Tim MacMahon discussed how the Pelicans' asking price for Murphy may be preventing a trade.

"Trey Murphy has constantly been in trade rumors, but I've never actually heard anything about him ever actually getting close to getting traded," Windhorst noted.

MacMahon noted the Pelicans have never gotten close to trading Murphy because their asking price has been comparable to "first-born children."

"His minutes and scoring are down this year," Windhorst added. "He'll still have a lot of value, but maybe not the value that [the Pelicans] think."

NBA insider Marc Stein previously reported that the Pelicans have asked for three first-round picks in exchange for Murphy.

New Orleans seems reluctant to trade the 26-year-old despite underwhelming performances from its current core group of players. The Pelicans have just two playoff appearances in the past eight seasons and have won less than 30 games in each of the past two seasons.

MacMahon also reported that some people within the NBA are wondering if the Pelicans will trade two-time All-Star Zion Williamson after the team's 4-10 record to start the season.

Pelicans point guard Dejounte Murray is another player who could be on the move after requesting a trade last week. The team released a statement Friday saying they "will evaluate potential trade opportunities that are in the best interest of our organization. released a statement.

Murphy will miss his fifth game on Monday due to patellar tendinopathy in both knees, but he has been a consistent starter while healthy. The sixth-year forward leads the team in minutes played (32.8) and ranks third on the team in points per game (15.6).

After the 2026-27 season, Murphy will have two years left on the four-year, $112,000,000 contract extension he signed in 2025, per Spotrac .

articles.body:
Brooklyn Nets forward Josh Minott and Chicago Bulls forward Matas Buzelis were fined $25,000 by the NBA after making obscene gestures toward the fans the league announced Monday.

Minott's incident occurred at the end of the Nets' 129-110 road loss to the Memphis Grizzlies on Saturday.

Buzelis' occurred that same evening, and came with 11:19 left in the Bulls' 117-106 win over the Minnesota Timberwolves, per the NBA.

Buzelis' incident was caught on the broadcast. After hitting a free throw, the forward flipped off someone in the crowd.

Minott's obscene gesture occurred after the game ended, per the NBA's release. Video of his gesture wasn't immediately available.

Minott played just 1:46 minutes in the contest, going 0-for-1 from the floor. He was also responsible for a turnover.

The NBA did not announce additional details regarding Minott's gesture, though it may have come immediately after the game, when Minott threw up — and bricked — a final second 3-ball while down by 19.

Minott, 23, has seen his role reduced by a fair amount this season. After a midseason trade brought him to the Nets last season, Minott played in 16 games with the team, averaging 19.3 minutes a game.

In nine games this season, Minott is averaging just 6.7 minutes per contest.

articles.title: Women's basketball AP poll: South Carolina solidifies No. 1 ranking with win over USC as UConn stumbles again
articles.summary: South Carolina beat JuJu Watkins and USC on Sunday afternoon in a thrilling battle for the "Real SC" title.
articles.body:
South Carolina is the clear No. 1 team in the country. Sunday afternoon's win over JuJu Watkins and USC proved that.

The Gamecocks beat Watkins and the Trojans in a thrilling battle for the "Real SC" title in South Carolina for yet another ranked win already this season. The Gamecocks, who also beat Maryland and North Carolina in the opening week of the season, held onto their No. 1 ranking in the latest Associated Press poll that was released on Monday.

Tessa Johnson dropped a career-high 28 points in the win on Sunday, and Joyce Edwards had a double-double with 20 points and 10 rebounds. And while they lost, Watkins and the Trojans were right there until the end. Watkins had 25 points in the outing, and the Trojans cut the lead to just a single possession in the final minute.

The loss only moved USC down one spot to No. 4 in this week's poll. Michigan remained at No. 2, Louisville jumped to No. 3 and Duke held at No. 5.

The big question this week, though, has to do with Geno Auriemma's UConn group in Storrs. The Huskies looked bad on Sunday afternoon in their matchup with Louisville . The Cardinals rolled to an 18-point win behind a 21-point outing from Imani Berry, which kept them a perfect 6-0 on the season. That moved them up to four spots into the top five. UConn shot just 34% from the field in the loss, and had four total bench points. The Huskies now sit at No. 7.

The loss was UConn's second already this season after an 11-point loss at Michigan in the opening week. While two losses shouldn't derail a season, things won't get any easier for UConn in its non-conference slate . The Huskies will go up against top-ranked South Carolina, No. 5 Duke, No. 18 Maryland, No. 13 Notre Dame, Tennessee and No. 9 LSU all before Big East play gets going. That's a brutal slate, one that may end up hurting them come NCAA tournament seeding time if Auriemma isn't able to right the ship.

While it's hard to count him out, considering the dominant run he's been on since taking over at UConn, this season hasn't gotten off to the best start for Auriemma.

articles.title: Detenido en Nigeria un jugador de baloncesto con 34 kilos de cannabis
articles.standfirst: El estadounidense Greene Da'monte Khiree, de 28 años, dice ser profesional en Tailandia
articles.summary: El estadounidense Greene Da'monte Khiree, de 28 años, dice ser profesional en Tailandia
articles.body: Las autoridades nigerianas detuvieron en el Aeropuerto Internacional Murtala Muhammed de Lagos (suroeste) a un estadounidense de 28 años que asegura ser jugador profesional de baloncesto en Tailandia por intentar introducir casi 34 kilos de cannabis, informó la Agencia Nacional Antidrogas de Nigeria (NDLEA, en inglés). El detenido, identificado como Greene Da'monte Khiree y natural de Savannah, en el estado estadounidense de Georgia, llegó el pasado 11 de noviembre a Lagos en un vuelo de Emirates procedente de Tailandia con escala en Dubái, según un comunicado de la NDLEA que recogen este lunes medios locales. Los agentes de la NDLEA sometieron al sospechoso a vigilancia tras recibir información de inteligencia y observaron que abandonó sus dos maletas facturadas antes de intentar salir del aeropuerto únicamente con su equipaje de mano. Los agentes lo detuvieron posteriormente en el aparcamiento del aeropuerto y registraron las dos maletas abandonadas, que llevaban etiquetas con su nombre. En su interior encontraron 32 paquetes con un total de 33,95 kilos de 'Loud', una potente variedad de cannabis. Khiree afirmó durante el interrogatorio que vive en Tailandia desde octubre de 2025, donde asegura jugar profesionalmente al baloncesto, y que había viajado a Nigeria de vacaciones para establecer contactos relacionados con su carrera deportiva. Sin embargo, la NDLEA señaló que un examen forense de su teléfono móvil encontró información que apunta a que conocía y estaba implicado en la operación de narcotráfico. La detención formó parte de una serie de operaciones anunciadas este domingo por la agencia antidrogas nigeriana en diferentes puntos del país. Ese mismo 11 de noviembre, también en el aeropuerto de Lagos, los agentes interceptaron 25,05 kilos de metanfetamina ocultos en paquetes de cereales que llegaron de Sudáfrica y detuvieron a un ciudadano nigeriano de 56 años. La NDLEA ha intensificado en los últimos meses sus operaciones contra redes nacionales e internacionales de narcotráfico, incluidas investigaciones sobre laboratorios clandestinos de metanfetamina en el país. El pasado septiembre, las autoridades nigerianas anunciaron la detención del mexicano Arturo Carrera Loaiza, al que vincularon con una red de laboratorios clandestinos de metanfetamina, dentro de una investigación que también llevó al arresto de otros ciudadanos mexicanos y nigerianos.

articles.title: 2026-27 NBA News, Injury Updates Nov. 16: Stephen Curry injured, Dejounte Murray makes trade request
articles.summary: Maybe one of these weeks I can write a summary that doesn't start with critical injuries.
articles.body:
Welcome to our weekly Monday Morning NBA notebook, a quick hit of NBA news and injuries from around the league to catch you up on what happened in the past week. Maybe one of these weeks I can write a summary that doesn't start with critical injuries.

The Golden State Warriors have been one of the great stories of the young season, with rookie Yaxel Landeborg grabbing headlines and winning games. The Warriors have beaten the Lakers, Timberwolves and Nuggets at points this season.

But this was still Stephen Curry's team, and his throwback start — 27.8 points per game, shooting 45.3% from 3-point range — is the foundation of all that winning. Now he is out with an oblique abdominal tear and will be re-evaluated in a couple of weeks, but reportedly could miss more like a month. In the game where he got injured and the game he missed so far, the Warriors got blown out. It might be a rough few weeks coming up in the Bay Area.

Caleb Wilson hasn't been the best rookie out of this class so far this young season, but he's been the most entertaining, averaging 18.9 points and 6.2 rebounds a game. More importantly, he gives the Bulls and their fans a real direction for the future after too many years of mediocrity (at best).

Now he is out 4-6 weeks with a hand fracture. Which just takes the air out of the sails in Chicago. It shouldn't impact winning or (more often) losing, they have been about the same with him on or off the court this season, but he brought a joy to the Bulls that is going to be missing for a bit.

We have our first trade request of the season : Dejounte Murray's agent (Rich Paul of Klutch Sports) told the New Orleans Pelicans Murray wants to be moved, something the Pelicans came out and confirmed.

When the Pelicans traded for Murray in the summer of 2024 it seemed like a good move on paper, he was the kind of guard who could bring together a talented roster that wasn't quite fitting with Zion Williamson, Trey Murphy III and others. It didn't work out that way, as he ruptured his Achilles that first season in New Orleans and missed the majority of his first two seasons there.

Jeremiah Fears is the point guard of the future in New Orleans, and he and Murray do not mesh well as a backcourt. This is best for everyone. That said, after injuries and a couple of down years because of it, the market for Murray is not going to bring a big return, so don't be surprised if this drags out into 2027 and closer to the February trade deadline.

The NBA is going to take its talents to South Beach.

The 2028 NBA All-Star Game will be in Miami, the first time the NBA's midseason showcase has been in the city since 1990 (Magic Johnson was your MVP that year). Miami has everything the NBA wants in a venue — warm weather, plenty of hotel rooms for fans, and players love the city and aren't looking for an excuse not to attend/skip town early — but the game traditionally falls on Presidents Day weekend, which is also when the city hosts the massive Miami International Boat Show. That show took up hotel and convention space the NBA needed, but in 2028 the boat show is moving back a weekend, reports the Miami Herald. The NBA stepped into that gap.

This is a win for everybody — Miami was made for this game.

• Cooper Flagg making history. Flagg is having a "he has arrived" season — looking every bit a top 15 player in the world already — and this past week he made history: Flagg passed LeBron James to be the teenager with the most 40+ point games in league history, and he also passed Kobe Bryant and now has scored the second most points as a teenager. He turns 20 next month.

• Lauri Markkanen is out with a wrist injury. Utah has dropped 12 straight, and this isn't helping matters: He has a non-displaced fracture in his right hand and will miss about a month (until mid-December). It likely means more touches for Darryn Peterson and Ace Bailey. • In the Jayson Tatum vs. Jaylen Brown showdown, Paul George was the star, reminding everyone he is still very good at basketball (and the Celtics got a convincing win). If he is healthy in April and May, the Celtics are a playoff threat in the East.

• The Bulls' Matas Buzelis and the Nets Josh Minott each have been fined $25,000 by the league for "making an obscene gesture towards the spectator stands." As a rule, the NBA frowns on players flipping off paying customers.

• Sacramento added veteran center Mason Plumlee to the roster. The Kings have a lot of centers on the roster, but that's not working as planned: Domantas Sabonis starts but is slumping, the future at the five may be Maxime Raynaud but he is injured, then there is Dylan Cardwell and, for small-ball lineups, Precious Achiuwa. Plumlee is not going to see a ton of minutes but the Kings could use the mentor.

articles.title: LeBron James Injury Update, Latest on 76ers Star's Status vs. Nets
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James won't play against the Brooklyn Nets on the road on Monday night.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James won't play against the Brooklyn Nets on the road on Monday night.

Per the Associated Press , James will miss the second half of the 76ers' back-to-back as he manages his low back and sciatica injury.

Ahead of James missing Monday's contest, ESPN's Dave McMenamin reported that the veteran "has asked coaches to be patient with him as he expects to find his rhythm and get his conditioning in line by December as he ramps up."

James missed his team's 123-112 home win against the Toronto Raptors on Nov. 12 because of the same injury .

He previously sat a pair of games on Oct. 25 and Oct. 31 . Of note, both matchups were part of back-to-back sets. The designations were injury management for low back pain/sciatica.

James missed the first 14 games of the 2025-26 NBA season, when he was a member of the Los Angeles Lakers, with sciatica on his right side .

The 41-year-old is playing in his 24th NBA season. The four-time NBA MVP and four-time NBA champion has averaged 15.1 points, 7.2 rebounds and 6.9 assists in 11 contests for an 11-3 76ers team fighting for the top spot in the Eastern Conference in the early going.

James has obviously played an integral part in the team's early success. Without him, the 76ers have turned to Dean Wade to join the starting lineup.

articles.title: 'Surreal,' Carmelo Anthony's Son Kiyan Dishes About Playing at MSG in Syracuse's Loss to St. John's
articles.summary: Syracuse guard Kiyan Anthony made his Madison Square Garden debut during Sunday's 79-62 loss against the St. John's Red Storm.
articles.body:
Syracuse guard Kiyan Anthony made his Madison Square Garden debut during Sunday's 79-62 loss against the St. John's Red Storm.

Although it was his first time playing a game in the arena, Anthony spent much of his childhood sitting courtside in Madison Square Garden watching his father, NBA Hall of Fame forward Carmelo Anthony.

This time, the tables were turned: Kiyan was on the court, and Carmelo was in the stands watching.

"It was surreal for me for a moment," Anthony said afterward at his locker, per Mike Fitzpatrick of the Associated Press. "Kind of just seeing, now my dad is watching me play from courtside as opposed to me watching him."

Carmelo spent seven seasons with the New York Knicks and produced plenty of iconic moments in Madison Square Garden, where he battled against all-time greats like Kobe Bryant, LeBron James and Kevin Durant. Those moments have stuck with his son, who reflected on those memories after the game.

"You don't forget those things," Anthony said late Sunday night, per Syracuse.com's Donna Ditota .

Syracuse coach Gerry McNamara sent Anthony into the game with 11:42 left in the first half and told him the offense would work through him, according to Ditota.

Although his team ultimately fell short, Anthony came off the bench and scored a team-high 17 points on 7-of-12 shooting in 27 minutes and 47 seconds. He also added four assists and two rebounds.

The 6-foot-5 sophomore has averaged 16 points, 1.1 assists and 1.5 rebounds through the first four games of the season.

articles.title: Jayson Tatum Dishes on Michael Jordan Relationship in New Video amid Celtics' Success
articles.summary: Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum has led the team to an 11-2 start this season, and he has one of the greatest players of all time in his corner.
articles.body:
Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum has led the team to an 11-2 start this season, and he has one of the greatest players of all time in his corner.

Tatum, who has been signed to the Jordan Brand since 2019, spoke to Boardroom's Speedy Morman about his relationship with the great Michael Jordan.

"I got to hang out with him this summer one day. We had lunch for like five, six hours. ... We just talked about any and everything," Tatum said at the 26:00 mark. "The thing about him is, he wants you to reach out and ask him questions or get insight or things like that. He's obviously Michael Jordan, but as cool as somebody at Michael Jordan's level could be, he's that guy."

Jordan has stayed out of the spotlight for the past few years, but it's clear that his influence on the game has endured. For Tatum, his mentorship has been an invaluable part of his career.

"His name in my phone is Uncle Mike," Tatum said. "So it was like I was just kicking it with my uncle for five, six hours, and we were just chillin'."

articles.title: 'Fishy S--t Going On' Jayson Tatum Talks Team USA Benching by Steve Kerr at 2024 Paris Olympics
articles.summary: Jayson Tatum was largely a role player who didn't even play in two 2024 Paris Olympics contests for the United States, and he reflected on that reality during an interview with Boardroom.
articles.body:
Jayson Tatum was largely a role player who didn't even play in two 2024 Paris Olympics contests for the United States, and he reflected on that reality during an interview with Boardroom.

After revealing head coach Steve Kerr told him he needed to stay patient, he added (19:50 mark), "I remember sitting on the bench, and once I didn't get in the first quarter, I was like, 'Oh, some fishy s--t going on.' That's when it kind of hit me like, 'Oh, that's what he was trying to tell me.'"

Tatum appeared in four of the Americans' six games in the tournament, which was the fewest of anyone on the team except for Tyrese Haliburton. Haliburton appeared in three games and famously joked about his role in winning the gold medal:

As for Tatum, he averaged 17.8 minutes per game in his Olympic appearances and did not play in the close semifinals win over Serbia.

It was a rather shocking development seeing how it was the summer after he helped lead the Boston Celtics to the NBA championship. He was also an All-NBA First-Team selection and finished sixth in MVP voting during the 2023-24 campaign.

Tatum was clearly on the short list of the best players in the league at the time of the Olympics and figured to be a key part in the team's run to the gold medal.

Instead, he was largely relegated to the bench in the key moments, which became a talking point during the Games.

Following the Olympics, Tatum told Jared Weiss of The Athletic the situation "was challenging" despite the team prevailing.

"It was a lot," he said. "In the age of social media, you see everything. You see all the tweets and the people on the podcasts and people on TV giving their opinion on whether they thought it was a good decision or it was an outrageous decision or whatever. Obviously, I wanted to contribute more, and I've never been in (this) situation. I started playing basketball at (age) three at the YMCA, and I've never not played, so it was different and it was challenging."

He once again discussed the benching during this latest interview, and it continues to be a storyline when reflecting on the experience.

articles.summary: Los azulgranas palian las bajas en el juego exterior con el base francés de 25 años y 1,96 metros, que no ha encontrado hueco en la NBA esta temporada
articles.body: En una operación relámpago, el Barcelona ha cerrado el fichaje de Killian Hayes, base de 25 años y 1,96 metros nacido en Florida pero con nacionalidad francesa que esta temporada no ha encontrado hueco en la NBA después de que los Kings no hicieran efectiva la opción que tenían sobre él. Los azulgranas se mueven con rapidez para paliar los problemas físicos que tienen en posiciones exteriores con Kevin Punter, Umoja Gibson y de un Juan Núñez que no termina de coger ritmo. Hayes, cuyo nombre ha sonado en las últimas temporadas como opción para regresar a Europa, donde se formó, concretamente en el Cholet francés. Este mismo verano, el base había sido tentado por varios equipos de Euroliga y ahora por fin se decide a dar el paso. Por físico, capacidades defensivas y visión de juego, puede marcar diferencias, aunque habrá que ver su encaje en este Barcelona que ahora va al alza. Se trata de unos los agentes libres con mejor cartel. El acuerdo entre el jugador y el Barça, adelantado por Michael Scotto, de 'HoopsHype', incluye una cláusula de salida que le permitiría regresar a la NBA, donde ha militado las seis últimas temporadas pasando por los Pistons, los Nets y los Kings sin llegar a mostrar todo el potencial que se le intuía cuando fue seleccionado como en el séptimo lugar del draft de 2020. En 239 partidos en la competición estadounidense, Hayes tuvo medias de 7,9 puntos con un discreto 28,0% en triples, 2,9 rebotes y 5,0 asistencias. articles.title: 5-Star Adan Diggs Makes Commitment Decision Between Arizona, Kentucky and More CBB Teams
articles.summary: The future of Arizona men's basketball got brighter Monday.
articles.body:
The future of Arizona men's basketball got brighter Monday.

That is because highly regarded recruit Adan Diggs chose the Wildcats over Arkansas, Kentucky and USC, among others.

Diggs is a 5-star prospect, the No. 6 overall player and the No. 1 combo guard in the 2027 recruiting class, per 247Sports' composite rankings.

He took official visits to Arizona, Arkansas and Kentucky, as well as an unofficial visit to USC. Ultimately, though, he chose the Big 12 program and previously discussed what stood out about his future basketball home.

"The way (Tommy Lloyd) runs his program sticks out," Diggs said, per Eric Bossi of 247Sports. "He's a coach who trusts his players to trust his system. He kind of lets his players do what they need to do, rock out and he knows that each guy in the group knows what they can do and how they need to fill their roles."

Diggs is someone who can fill a number of roles with the ability to impact the game multiple ways.

He averaged 18.3 points, 6.1 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.8 steals and 0.8 blocks per game in the EYBL. Adam Finkelstein of 247Sports pointed out how the guard is a "three-range scoring threat" who can attack the basket off the dribble, get out in transition, hit pull-up shots and extend his offensive arsenal beyond the arc.

Finkelstein also highlighted Diggs' defense and rebounding capability, especially as someone who plays in the backcourt.

Arizona has no shortage of momentum and is coming off a Final Four appearance last season. It was also its third straight Sweet 16 appearance under Lloyd, and this season's team is talented enough to challenge for another deep run in March.

The best way to maintain that momentum and compete for future Final Four appearances is by having success on the recruiting trail and in the transfer portal. Diggs is a significant addition and one that is all the more important because Lloyd convinced him to join the fold over a number of other high-profile programs.

The incoming prospect is a future building block and someone who will likely play a key role in the rotation from the moment he arrives on campus.

articles.title: Purdue baseball players sue NCAA seeking fifth year of eligibility
articles.summary: Three Purdue baseball players are suing the NCAA, seeking a fifth season of eligibility for the 2026-27 season.
articles.body:
WEST LAFAYETTE, IN — Three Purdue University baseball players are suing the university and the NCAA in an attempt to gain a fifth year of eligibility for the upcoming 2026-27 season.

Sam Flores, Brandon Rogers and Jake Kramer, seniors at Purdue, allege in a lawsuit filed Friday in Tippecanoe Superior Court 1 along with 42 other collegiate athletes across the country that they have been unfairly denied a fifth season of their respective sports because of the NCAA's rule change allowing all those graduating from high school after 2022 to compete in five seasons without needing to "redshirt."

"The NCAA's application of this bylaw to Plaintiffs unfairly limits the number of games they can participate in during their 'five-year eligibility window' and unfairly denies them a benefit — a fifth season of competition — that the NCAA now affords to every other class of student-athlete," the lawsuit said. "NCAA athletes have a reasonable expectation that they will be treated fairly by the NCAA and that NCAA rules will be applied consistently, regardless of the athlete's background before they attend an NCAA school and regardless of the year in which they graduated from high school."

In October, a Clark Circuit Court judge granted former Purdue basketball star Trey Kaufman-Renn a sixth season of eligibility, after he received a temporary restraining order in that case to allow him to move forward with finding a team for the current season. By late October, Kaufman-Renn announced he'd signed with the Kansas men's basketball team.

The newest eligibility lawsuit is one of several filed in recent weeks against the NCAA by college athletes looking for one more season. Lawyers for Flores, Rogers and Kramer argue that the current seniors, who were 2022 high school graduates, have been competing against older, stronger and more experienced players who were allowed to play five years or more because of a COVID-era waiver.

The lawsuit argues that by not allowing the current seniors a fifth season, the NCAA is violating its contractual agreement with its member schools, of which all Division I athletes are intended third-party beneficiaries.

"While it is too late for most athletes who competed in the 2025-26 academic year to secure roster spots to compete in 2026-27, Plaintiffs all believe they still have opportunities to play in 2026-27 if they can obtain immediate injunctive relief from this Court," the lawsuit said.

Flores, Rogers and Kramer said in the lawsuit that if they were granted a fifth season of eligibility, they would remain at Purdue.

In response, the NCAA noted that the "majority" of the other plaintiffs are also parties in pending lawsuits in other states and asked the judge to weigh that before granting a temporary restraining order.

In July, a group of student-athletes filed a lawsuit in Davidson County, Tennessee, in an attempt to gain a fifth season of eligibility. Several of the students from that case, the NCAA said, have been named in the current Purdue lawsuit, too.

In August, the Tennessee Court of Appeals granted the NCAA's motion to stay the injunction pending appeal, making the players in that case ineligible.

The NCAA also pointed to a similar case filed over the summer in Georgia, where the Georgia Court of Appeals also ruled in favor of the NCAA, making those students, also named in the Purdue lawsuit, ineligible.

Jillian Ellison is a reporter for the Journal & Courier. She can be reached via email at jellison@usatodayco.com.

articles.title: NBA’s latest update shows just how far Luka Doncic is ahead of the pack
articles.summary: Hollywood loves a good showman, and Luka Doncic is giving fans of the Los Angeles Lakers everything they could have hoped for with another magical campaign....
articles.body:
Hollywood loves a good showman, and Luka Doncic is giving fans of the Los Angeles Lakers everything they could have hoped for with another magical campaign.

Doncic has looked every bit the leading man, carrying the Lakers to an eight-game winning streak and a 12-2 record, tied with the San Antonio Spurs for the NBA's best record. He shone with 43 points in Los Angeles' win against the Phoenix Suns , 131-123, at PHX Arena on Sunday.

He is averaging a league-leading 39.0 points , way ahead of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander of the Oklahoma City Thunder, Giannis Antetokounmpo of the Miami Heat, Victor Wembanyama of the San Antonio Spurs, and Stephen Curry of the Golden State Warriors.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The 27-year-old Doncic, a two-time scoring champion, has made everything look easy with his unparalleled shot-making. He is also doing it efficiently, averaging 48.6% from the field, including a career-high 40.6% from long range.

The six-time All-Star has reached 40 points in five of their last seven games, including a season-high 53 points against the Portland Trail Blazers in the NBA Cup on Friday. He has not scored fewer than 23 points this season.

In a report from BasketNews, coach JJ Redick shared how Doncic prepared extensively in the offseason.

"He's great physically. The guy worked his butt off all summer on staying in shape and actually ran this summer. He actually did sprints and stuff and came into camp in fantastic shape," said Redick.

"We've seen him literally every day in camp just incrementally get more and more in rhythm."

The Lakers will try to extend their hot streak against the Charlotte Hornets on Tuesday.

articles.title: Elite, 5-star guard Haylen Ayers announces commitment to Vanderbilt
articles.summary: Haylen Ayers is a four-time Miss Basketball winner in Tennessee and the fourth-ranked player in the 2027 class.
articles.body:
Haylen Ayers has been regarded as one of the best girls basketball players in the country since she first began playing varsity ball as an eighth grader.

Now entering her senior season, Tennessee's top basketball star has made her college decision, and she decided to go to the school where he mom made a name for herself.

On Monday, Nov. 16, Ayers announced her commitment to Shea Ralph and the Vanderbilt Commodore s. Her decision came down to two schools and she chose Vanderbilt over UConn.

Vanderbilt has consistently been a factor in Ayers' recruitment as her mom Ashley was a standout with the Commodores from 1999 to 2003.

This year, Ayers has the opportunity to do something that no player in Tennessee has ever done by winning her fourth consecutive Miss Basketball award. She's tied with Ohio State guard and former Ensworth standout Jaloni Cambridge with three straight but Cambridge transferred to Montverde Academy (FL) for her senior season.

The only season where Ayers was not named as the Division II-A Miss Basketball was her eighth-grade season. That year she averaged 14.7 points per game.

As a freshman, Ayers won her first Miss Basketball award during a season that saw her average 18.6 points, leading USJ to its first girls basketball state title.

The following year, she averaged 21.8 points and eight rebounds while leading the Lady Bruins to the DII-A semifinals. Last year, she averaged 21.9 points and 6.9 rebounds, leading the team once again to a Division II-A championship appearance.

As well as being the state's top girls basketball prospect, Ayers is also one of the best softball players in the state, holding numerous Power Four offers.

Ayers is ranked as the No. 4 overall prospect in the latest USA TODAY girls basketball composite rankings and the No. 2 shooting guard prospect in the class. She joins a Vanderbilt class that boasts a commitment from the state's No. 2 overall prospect and a fellow five-star in Clarksville Christian power forward Lauren Hassell.

articles.title: LSU Guard MiLaysia Fulwiley Absent for the No. 9 Tigers' Win over Troy After Recent Arrest
articles.summary: BATON ROUGE, La (AP) — LSU senior guard MiLaysia Fulwiley, who was arrested after allegedly attempting to flee a traffic stop Saturday night, was not with the No. 9 Tigers for their 116-70 win over Troy on Monday night.
articles.body:
BATON ROUGE, La (AP) — LSU senior guard MiLaysia Fulwiley, who was arrested after allegedly attempting to flee a traffic stop Saturday night, was not with the No. 9 Tigers for their 116-70 win over Troy on Monday night.

Florida transfer Laila Reynolds, who came off the bench for the first four games of this season, started in Fulwiley's place.

LSU coach Kim Mulkey did not address Fulwiley's status on Sunday or before the game on Monday, and it remained unclear to those outside the locker room whether she would be with the team until the Tigers came out for pre-game warm-ups.

"I truly think we gave a statement," Mulkey said after her team's win. "The university did and that's all I'm willing to say right until I gather more information."

The university stated on Sunday that it was aware of the arrest but would not comment further on a pending legal matter.

East Baton Rouge District Attorney Hillar Moore said Monday he was still awaiting reports on the matter from the law enforcement departments involved.

The traffic stop occurred around the time the Texas vs. LSU football game was ending on Saturday night.

The Louisiana State Police, who assist with traffic flow around 102,000-seat Tiger Stadium on football game days, have said they intend to collect and make available all available video footage from body and dashboard cameras. Police also indicated they would seek security camera footage from buildings in the area where the stop occurred and where Fulwiley was ultimately taken into custody.

Authorities allege that an officer tried to stop the 21-year-old Fulwiley after observing her weaving through traffic, and that she drove away from the scene, the right front side of her vehicle striking a police vehicle.

She allegedly sought to cut through a store parking lot before her vehicle was blocked by responding police.

Fulwiley was booked into East Baton Rouge Parish Prison on charges including aggravated battery, flight from an officer, aggravated assault and resisting an officer.

Fulwiley is averaging 17.8 points per game this season and scored a season-high 23 points during LSU's 101-37 victory over Denver on Friday.

articles.title: Haylen Ayers, 2027 five-star, commits to Vanderbilt women's basketball over UConn
articles.summary: Haylen Ayers will follow in her mother's footsteps after committing to Vanderbilt women's basketball on Nov. 16.
articles.body:
University School of Jackson senior guard Haylen Ayers announced her commitment to Vanderbilt basketball on Nov. 16 at USJ's Blankenship Theater.

Ayers, a five-star recruit according to the 247Sports Composite , chose Vanderbilt over UConn. She also had offers from Duke, Kentucky and Texas, among others.

Ayers is ranked as the top player in Tennessee and the No. 3 player nationally in the Class of 2027. Ayers plays softball for the Bruins and was ranked as the No. 22 softball recruit nationally by Rivals .

Ayers averaged 21.9 points, 6.9 rebounds, 2.9 assists and 2.6 steals while leading the Bruins to the state title game as a junior. She is a three-time Division II-A Miss Basketball winner and led the Bruins to a championship in 2024.

Ayers commitment to Vanderbilt comes with a family connection. Her mother, Ashley Ayers (née McElhiney), played four seasons with the Commodores from 1999 to 2003 and was a two-time All-SEC selection. Ayers' mother was teammates with Ashley Earley, who is now an assistant coach on Shea Ralph's staff.

Ayers is the second Class of 2027 recruit who will join Vanderbilt. Four-star forward Lauren Hassell ― the second-ranked player in Tennessee who plays at Clarksville Christian and is the daughter of former Austin Peay great Trenton Hassell ― signed to Vandy on Nov. 12.

Vanderbilt finished 29-5 in 2025-26 behind the play of Mikayla Blakes, who averaged 27 points and 4.5 assists as a sophomore. The Commodores are off to a 4-1 start this season.

articles.title: 5-Star PG Cayden Daughtry Makes Commitment Decision Between Arkansas, FSU, Miami, Louisville
articles.summary: John Calipari landed a future difference-maker for the Arkansas men's basketball program Monday.
articles.body:
John Calipari landed a future difference-maker for the Arkansas men's basketball program Monday.

As ESPN's Jeff Borzello reported, guard Cayden Daughtry committed to the Razorbacks as part of their 2027 recruiting class. According to 247Sports' composite rankings, Daughtry is a 5-star prospect, the No. 4 overall player and the No. 2 point guard in his class.

While Daughtry has been highly regarded and didn't exactly sneak up on anyone, he joins Arkansas with plenty of momentum.

Borzello noted he "put together one of the great July runs of all time" by taking home a Peach Jam championship and a U17 World Cup gold medal. What's more, he won the Peach Jam MVP by averaging a stunning 32.3 points and 6.1 assists per game.

It highlighted how he can take over games on the offense end and is a willing facilitator whenever opposing defenses focus too much attention on him.

That caught the eye of a number of college programs, as he chose Arkansas over the likes of Florida State, Miami and Louisville.

Adam Finkelstein of 247Sports had high praise for Daughtry, calling him the "most skilled player in high school basketball" thanks to his ball-handling, ability to hit from deep, floaters in the lane and overall playmaking from the point guard spot.

Calipari is no stranger to landing high-impact point guards on the recruiting trail, and it would be anything but a surprise if Daughtry is a key playmaker for the Razorbacks as soon as his freshman season.

Arkansas is coming off back-to-back Sweet 16 appearances and now have a future difference-maker who could help it take the next step for another deep run in March.

articles.title: Heat star Bam Adebayo leaves win over Rockets early with hip injury
articles.summary: Despite losing Bam Adebayo in the second half, the Heat still rolled to a 128-110 win over the Rockets on Monday night.
articles.body:
Bam Adebayo left Monday night's contest against the Houston Rockets early with an apparent hip injury.

The Miami Heat star did not take the court to start the second half of their 128-110 win over the Rockets at the Kaseya Center on Monday, and was instead replaced by Andrew Wiggins to open the third quarter. It didn't appear as if anything happened to Adebayo in the first half, but he was not spotted on the bench as play resumed.

Eventually, the Heat said he was questionable to return with right hip tightness. They then ruled him out for good in the fourth quarter. Further specifics of the injury are not yet known.

Adebayo finished the night with just four points and two assists while shooting 1-of-3 from the field. He entered the night averaging 19.5 points and 8.5 rebounds per contest this season.

While it's unclear how severe the injury is just yet, losing Adebayo for an extended amount of time would undoubtedly make a major impact on the Heat. But despite losing him, the Heat still managed to roll to a convincing win over the Rockets.

Miami led nearly the entire way on Monday night. The Heat carried a 16-point lead into the locker room at halftime and just cruised the rest of the way to secure the 18-point win. Giannis Antetokounmpo led the way with 20 points, 16 rebounds and six assists. Klay Thompson added 17 points after going 5-of-10 from the 3-point line, and Wiggins had 17 points and five rebounds after stepping in for Adebayo in the second half. The Heat have now won five straight, and sit at 8-6 on the season.

Alperen Sengun led the Rockets with 23 points and seven rebounds. Kevin Durant finished with 22 points, and Jabari Smith Jr. had 12 points and 10 rebounds. The loss dropped them to 11-4 on the year.

articles.title: Embiid, Brown Shine as 76ers Beat Nets With LeBron Out, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Maxey, More
articles.summary: Joel Embiid delivered his highest-scoring performance of the early NBA season to lead the LeBron James-less Philadelphia 76ers to a 134-123 victory over the Brooklyn Nets.
articles.body:
Joel Embiid delivered his highest-scoring performance of the early NBA season to lead the LeBron James-less Philadelphia 76ers to a 134-123 victory over the Brooklyn Nets.

Embiid eclipsed the 30-point mark for the first time this season on the second leg of a back-to-back in which James sat due to injury management.

Jaylen Brown produced his second consecutive 30-point game and third 30-point performance of November to star alongside Embiid.

Embiid played well from the start of Monday's game at the Barclays Center.

The Sixers center went off for 13 points in the first quarter.

Embiid had 24 of his 34 points by halftime, as the Sixers opened up a 19-point advantage at the break.

Embiid was the first-half star for the Sixers, but Jaylen Brown contributed across the stat columns as well. The first-year Sixer recorded a double-double by halftime.

The Sixers let the Nets creep back into the game in the third quarter. Brooklyn posted 36 points in the third.

The Nets played well down the stretch to keep Philadelphia's starters on the floor for most of the fourth quarter.

Embiid delivered the dagger with a minute left in the game with a three-pointer from the right corner.

Embiid, Brown and Tyrese Maxey combined for 92 of Philadelphia's 135 points. Maxey and Brown combined to knock down seven three-pointers.

The victory moved the Sixers to 12-3 and it allowed them to take over first place in the Eastern Conference by a half-game over the Boston Celtics, who lost to the Orlando Magic on Monday. Orlando is Philadelphia's next opponent on Wednesday.

articles.title: Revolución en el marketing: el Heat-Bucks, la primera peripecia del GTA VI
articles.standfirst: El lanzamiento del popular videojuego despliega una gigantesca e inédita colaboración con la NBA: Miami 'tunea' su pabellón, pierde su nombre y cambiará su camiseta
articles.summary: El lanzamiento del popular videojuego despliega una gigantesca e inédita colaboración con la NBA: Miami 'tunea' su pabellón, pierde su nombre y cambiará su camiseta
articles.body: En una iniciativa nunca vista en la NBA, el partido Heat-Bucks de este miércoles 18 de noviembre en Miami servirá para promocionar el lanzamiento mundial de GTA VI, la famosa franquicia de videojuegos de acción y aventura en campo abierto publicada por Rockstar Games. El peculiar influjo de la saga, que es un fenómeno global con 465 millones de copias vendidas en su historia desde 2001, cambiará el aspecto del Kaseya Center, que tendrá múltiples referencias al universo GTA. Los Heat se llamarán por un día Vice City, en el primer cambio de identidad de la historia de un equipo NBA, y jugarán con un uniforme distinto como anticipo fantástico del inicio de la venta oficial del videojuego, que se producirá cinco horas después. El partido, que inicia una nueva era en el marketing deportivo, no es uno cualquiera de los 1.230 programados de temporada regular. Por primera vez en su carrera, una de las súper estrellas del campeonato, el griego Giannis Antetokounmpo, que jugó 13 temporadas en Milwaukee donde fue campeón en 2021 y dos veces MVP (2019 y 2020), se medirá a los Bucks. Salvando las distancias, en lo emocional podría ser algo parecido al primer partido de Michael Jordan frente a los Bulls, en Washington, en enero de 2002, en el inicio de la primera de las dos temporadas del G.O.A.T. con los Wizards. Sin gran interés deportivo (no es el mejor arranque de temporada para Heat, 8-6 y Bucks, el peor equipo del Este, 1-13), la dimensión morbosa de la cita (también para un héroe local Tyler Herro, que ahora juega en Milwaukee) sólo es un gran añadido al gigantesco envoltorio con el que GTA VI se presentará al mundo convirtiendo la experiencia de un partido NBA en un evento fascinante. Vice City jugará con un uniforme negro con ribetes rosa neón, una edición limitada de una camiseta diseñada por Nike y Cactus Jack (la firma de Travis Scott). Llevará el logo de Nike al revés, el escudo de GTA VI con unas palmeras y referencias al mapa de Miami en los dorsales. La ciudad ya siente el partido como un evento especial. Hay carteles en el aeropuerto y en el centro. Es un acontecimiento. La cancha del Kaseya Center estará ‘tuneada’ con los colores del vídeojuego. Se llamará ‘The Vice City Court’. Tendrá múltiples referencias al universo Grand Theft Auto con iconografía propia de GTA VI. La ambientación inmersiva del pabellón te meterá de lleno en el videojuego porque habrá vehículos reales en exposición en West Plaza, carteles luminosos, música ambiental que se escucha en el juego electrónico y puestos de comida rápida ambientados como las cadenas ficticias Burger Shot y Cluckin’Bell. Con semejante estrategia, casi lo de menos es el lanzamiento paralelo de una colección exclusiva de ropa, con camisetas, gorras y sudaderas inspiradas en la estética de GTA VI. La inédita colaboración va más allá que la ya habitual de Nickelodeon con la NFL, la alianza iniciada en 2021 junto a la cadena CBS para atraer al público infantil a los partidos de ‘football’. El colmo fue la aparición de 'Fondo de Bikini' en la retransmisión alternativa de la Super Bowl de 2024. Bob Esponja y Patricio Estrella aparecían como comentaristas virtuales del partido que ganaron los Chiefs a los 49ers. En 2027, en la Super Bowl, habrá un homenaje a Star Wars, en el 50 aniversario del estreno de la mítica saga galáctica. La NBA ya había tenido colaboraciones temáticas con Disney y con Marvel. El Heat-Bucks es dar un paso más. Si el jugador del GTA VI puede caminar, correr, nadar o robar cualquier vehículo del entorno para desplazarse por la ciudad y acudir a puntos marcados por el mapa, la primera de las múltiples peripecias estará en un partido real de la NBA. Una revolución.

articles.body:
Miami Heat star Giannis Antetokounmpo expects Wednesday's game against the Milwaukee Bucks to be "just another game."

The matchup will mark the first time Antetokounmpo will face his former team since the offseason trade that landed him in Miami. While speaking to reporters on Monday, he noted he hasn't found himself "being emotional" about the matchup.

Antetokounmpo also discussed his Bucks legacy as well as the trade:

The two-time MVP is in the midst of his first year with Miami after the Heat acquired him in a blockbuster trade with Milwaukee over the offseason.

Through his first 13 appearances with the Heat, he has averaged 28.9 points, 12.5 rebounds, 5.2 assists and 1.2 blocks per game. He had 29 points (while making eight of 11 field goals), 13 rebounds, six assists and three blocks in Monday's 128-110 victory over the Houston Rockets.

articles.title: LeBron James Denies Rumors That He Asked 76ers Coaches to Be 'Patient' in IG Photo
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers superstar LeBron James took to social media on Monday to deny a recent report saying that he asked the team's coaching staff to be "patient" with him to start the season.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers superstar LeBron James took to social media on Monday to deny a recent report saying that he asked the team's coaching staff to be "patient" with him to start the season.

ESPN's Dave McMenamin reported prior to Monday's game against the Brooklyn Nets that James "has asked coaches to be patient with him as he expects to find his rhythm and get his conditioning in line by December as he ramps up."

James, 41, sat out Monday night's game, which was the backend of a set of back-to-back games. Philadelphia pulled out a 135-123 victory over Brooklyn with James sidelined.

James has truly embraced the role of playmaker in Philadelphia, averaging 15.1 points, 6.9 assists and 7.2 rebounds per game. His vision, passing and leadership has been vital for the new-look Sixers, especially as the halfcourt offense has struggled at times to find a flow.

Nonetheless, the team has started 12-3 and looks like one of the NBA's true contenders this season.

James was one of many key additions for the Sixers in the offseason. Alongside his signing and the high-profile trade for Jaylen Brown, the team also signed Dean Wade, Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, who have all been important parts of the team's rotation.

Few teams boast the sort of talent Philly has in its starting 5, with James and Brown joining the talented trio of Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid and VJ Edgecombe.

articles.title: 76ers' Jaylen Brown injures head, hamstring in victory over Nets
articles.summary: Brown and Randle collided in the fourth quarter of Philadelphia's 135-123 win, leaving both men bleeding.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers forward Jaylen Brown briefly went down with a potential head injury after knocking heads with Brooklyn Nets forward Julius Randle. Though Brown was bleeding, he eventually returned to the game with a bandage on his head, and played a few more minutes of the 76ers' 135-123 win over the Nets.

The collision between Brown and Randle happened in the fourth quarter of Monday's matchup in Brooklyn, with Brown's forehead connecting with Randle's mouth. Both men were bleeding after the incident, though from different parts of the head.

Brown stayed down for a while, rolling onto his back and covering his face with his hands. The entire 76ers bench soon came out to surround him while he was tended to by trainers. Brown then received additional care on the bench, before returning to the game with a bandage on his head.

Brown eventually left again because of tightness in his left hamstring. He said he will have additional testing on both his head and his hamstring on Tuesday.

Randle, meanwhile, got his bloody lip stitched up off the court and returned to the game as well. Randle was called for the foul on the play, but because it wasn't a shooting foul, Brown did not need to attempt free throws.

At the time of the foul, Brown had scored 29 points and picked up 12 rebounds, thanks to a first-half double-double. He finished with 31 points, 13 rebounds and 4 assists in the 12-point victory.

Joel Embiid led both teams with 37 points, while Randle had 33 points for Brooklyn in the loss.
