articles.title: “JuJu Is A Better All-Around Player”: 5X NBA Champion Takes Savage Swipe At Caitlin Clark While Defending JuJu Watkins
articles.summary: Five-time NBA champion Ron Harper says JuJu Watkins and Caitlin Clark don’t have the same game, and the debate comes with a draft clock attached.
articles.body:
Every rising star gets measured against the last one. For JuJu Watkins, the yardstick has a name, and the name is Caitlin Clark.

On Monday, five-time NBA champion Ron Harper tried to end that debate. Replying to a lengthy post on X, Harper wrote, " They don't have the same game. "

One can shoot, Harper added, and Watkins is the better all-around player. He closed by telling people to stop the nonsense, in saltier language.

The post he answered argued that the hunt for the next Clark is a pipe dream. It praised Watkins as an exceptional talent. But it said Clark was an elite scorer, a generational playmaker, and an entire offense by herself.

Watkins scored 25 points on 8-of-20 shooting in USC's 89-85 loss to South Carolina. She hit 1 of 4 from three. CBC Sports also noted five turnovers.

Not everyone wanted to close the case. Analyst Jason Whitlock asked for patience. He said to check back on Watkins at season's end, and he liked how she looked on the road against a traditional powerhouse.

In 2025, Watkins won the Wooden Award and the Naismith, AP, and USBWA player of the year honors. As a freshman, she set the NCAA Division I freshman scoring record with 920 points. She also reached 1,000 career points in 38 games, the fastest in USC history. Most WNBA executives see her as a generational prospect.

Through four games, Watkins averages 24.5 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists, 3.3 steals, and 1.3 blocks. She shoots 45.9% from the field. All of it comes after an ACL tear that cost her the entire 2025-26 season.

Harper has stepped into Clark conversations before. After the fall to the Las Vegas Aces in the first round, he drew a line between the player and her crowd. He tweeted that he respects " her game but not her followers. "

Harper wants the player judged on the floor, not through the noise around her. Linda Cohn was asked on Yahoo Sports Daily whether Watkins can be compared to Clark.

Her answer was short: " Maybe after Caitlin Clark retires. "

Eddie Gonzalez, Kevin Durant's Boardroom co-host, said he loves Clark and Watkins alike. He added that fans can discuss other players without bringing Clark up every time.

What The Ron Harper Take Means For JuJu Watkins And The Tempo

The Toronto Tempo won the WNBA draft lottery on Sunday and will pick first on April 12. They went 11-33 in their inaugural season.

ESPN's Michael Voepel has Watkins going first in his mock draft from Friday, ahead of Notre Dame's Hannah Hidalgo and Texas' Madison Booker. Watkins has not declared, though. Because of the ACL injury, she has another season of college eligibility.

She wants an NCAA title before turning pro. Cohn noted she could earn more by staying in school another year. This season, Clark became the first WNBA player with back-to-back games of 30 points and 10 assists. In July, she posted 45 points and 10 assists against Seattle. Games she plays draw audiences about 2.6 times larger than a standard WNBA matchup.

Hidalgo is not waiting around, either. She opened her senior year on a tear, averaging 27.3 points, 7.7 rebounds, 5.0 assists and 5.0 steals for Notre Dame, which keeps the top of this class crowded.

Harper has made his case, and the comparisons will keep coming. What Watkins does at USC between now and April 12 will decide which question follows her next: when she turns pro, or whether she does at all.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown Says 'Trust the Process' and Joel Embiid Immediately Reacts in Funny Trending Video
articles.summary: Whether intentional or not, one postgame remark from Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown struck the perfect chord with teammate Joel Embiid.
articles.body:
Whether intentional or not, one postgame remark from Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown struck the perfect chord with teammate Joel Embiid.

The Sixers improved their record to 12-3 with a 135-123 win over the Brooklyn Nets on Tuesday. Brown told reporters after the victory it's important for the team, at what's still an early point in the NBA season, to "trust the journey, trust the process":

Referencing Philly's longtime motto drew a chuckle from a nearby Embiid.

Earnestly saying "trust the process" might be the point when Brown officially became a 76ers player.
